one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mumbai-based provider of turnkey trade show and exhibition booth solutions — custom-built and modular — with design done in-house and fabrication outsourced under company supervision, serving Indian and international exhibition hubs.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is engaged in the business of trade show and exhibition booth solutions, offering both custom-built and modular exhibition options. Design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations with professionals, while booth fabrication and related services are outsourced and carried out under the Company's supervision. Services extend from concept design and 3D visualization to project management, logistics, on-site supervision, fabrication, installation and post-event dismantling support, for B2B and B2C exhibitors across industries such as Industrial Machinery & Equipment, Building Materials, Furnishing & Decor, Chemicals, Media & Entertainment, Healthcare & Cosmetics and Food & Beverages.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light services model with a dual execution framework rather than owned manufacturing. Booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to subcontractors while design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations; all subcontractors are directly hired and managed by the Company and all subcontracted work is carried out under its active guidance and on-ground supervision, with supervisors physically present on-site for the full duration of the project. Both partial and full subcontracting models are used, and the Company also takes on subcontracted work from other firms. The outsourcing model runs a formal two-step process (vendor screening - define project requirements, identify potential vendors, pre-screening checklist covering GST/PAN and financial stability, RFP/RFQ, proposal evaluation, vendor interviews, due diligence and background checks including litigation/blacklisting, final selection and contracting, onboarding and governance; then project execution - project management tools, milestone work plan, daily status calls and on-site monitoring, final delivery and handover). The in-house model covers material requirement definition (plywood, commercial ply, nylon carpet rolls and other construction/finish items), vendor shortlisting, RFQ, quotation evaluation, purchase order issue, material delivery and inspection, payment processing and inventory recordkeeping. Revenue by execution mode (% of total revenue): Subcontract 90.89% / 92.11% / 75.48% / 64.40% and In-house 9.11% / 7.89% / 24.52% / 35.60% for the period ended Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23. Vendor and execution metrics (not cumulative), Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23: total active subcontractors globally (domestic and international) 53 / 36 / 29 / 22; projects executed with international local allies 125 / 69 / 49 / 20; projects executed domestically 307 / 312 / 207 / 205; total booths delivered globally 432 / 381 / 256 / 225; total repeat clients 63 / 27 / 28 / 48; average project turnaround time 3 to 30 days in every period. The Company states it does not own fabrication machinery or permanent event spaces and instead rents godowns, fabrication equipment, raw materials and temporary project sites project-by-project; materials are sourced locally in overseas markets to reduce logistics dependencies. Risk factors disclose that there are no executed registered formal arrangements with the outsourced subcontractors governing specifications, quality standards, sales estimates or packaging, and that foreign outsourcing adds FX, cross-border regulatory, geopolitical and logistical exposure. Registered office and both godowns are on leasehold premises. International client base grew 245% over the last three years, from 20 to 69 international clients; total booths delivered globally grew at a stated CAGR of 30.13% from FY23 to FY25.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- General economic conditions in India and changes in laws and regulations (stated key factor affecting results of operations)
- Changes in revenue mix, including geographic mix of revenues (stated key factor) - visible in the shift of domestic share from 99.39% in FY23 to 87.17% for the period ended February 28, 2026
- Changes in fiscal, economic or political conditions in India (stated key factor)
- Availability and cost of raw materials (stated key factor)
- Increased market fragmentation (stated key factor)
- Competition with existing and new entrants (stated key factor)
- Technology-related factor - the seventh stated key factor is cut off mid-word ('Technol...') in the routed extract and could not be captured in full
- No significant developments since February 28, 2026: in the opinion of the Board there have not arisen any significant developments or circumstances that materially or adversely affect, or are likely to affect, profitability, the value of assets or the ability to pay material liabilities within the next twelve months
- Working capital intensity is the sole operating use of Fresh Issue proceeds, and the disclosed Capital Turnover Ratio (revenue from operations / average working capital) fell from 50.63x in FY23 to 6.75x in FY25 and 4.17x for the period ended February 28, 2026, alongside a Current Ratio rising from 1.14 to 3.28 - i.e. a lengthening working capital cycle
- Operational performance indicators disclosed in the DRHP may not be derived from the Restated Financial Statements and may not have been audited or reviewed by the Statutory Auditor; investors are cautioned against undue reliance
- EBITDA as defined excludes other income and is before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortisation and exceptional items

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Deploy the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue towards funding the Company's working capital requirements and general corporate purposes
- List the Equity Shares on the EMERGE Platform of the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to enhance corporate image and brand visibility, provide liquidity to existing shareholders and create a public trading market
- Continue the dual execution model - combining outsourcing/subcontracting with in-house project execution - to balance quality control, scalability and cost efficiency across projects
- Maintain comprehensive control over the entire process from design through build by leveraging in-house production capabilities alongside a global network of trusted sub-contractors
- Continue delivering turnkey solutions aligned to international standards while adapting to local event formats and client preferences, using local collaborators to blend with cultural diversities and regional preferences
- Continue renting godowns or storage spaces temporarily at or near event locations as needed to ensure smooth execution and logistics

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed DRHP text discloses NO capacity, plant or capex expansion programme. The Fresh Issue objects are limited to (i) funding working capital requirements of the Company and (ii) general corporate purposes - there is no capex object, no new facility and no commissioning timeline. The Company's stated infrastructure model is deliberately asset-light: booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to subcontractors under Company supervision, the two godowns at Vasai/Virar (Maharashtra) and Madanayakanahally/Tumkur Road (Bengaluru, Karnataka) are rented and serve storage, logistics and fabrication support rather than owned manufacturing, and additional godown/storage space is rented temporarily at or near event sites as projects require. Geographic reach is described as already established rather than as a funded expansion plan - presence spanning India, Dubai, US, UK, Germany and other international regions, served through working relationships with local teams and a global network of sub-contractors; the accompanying disclosure shows international revenue rising from 0.61% of revenue from operations in FY23 to 12.83% for the period ended February 28, 2026, but the DRHP text provided states no forward target for it. The 'Our Business - Competitive Strengths' and business-strategy discussion referenced on page 195 is not included in the routed extract, so any expansion narrative contained there is not captured here.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established track record in a fragmented industry (stated qualitative factor for the Offer Price)
- Agile, asset-light business model enabling scalable growth (stated qualitative factor)
- Global execution framework enabled by established practices and local integration (stated qualitative factor)
- Brand-led booth design by skilled in-house marketing & branding team (stated qualitative factor)
- Over 12 years of experience executing both B2B and B2C-focused events, with end-to-end booth services adapted to client branding goals and regional regulations
- Dual execution model (outsourcing/subcontracting plus in-house execution) balancing quality control, scalability and cost efficiency, with a formal 8-step vendor screening process
- PAN-India presence across 15+ states plus operational ties in the US, UK, Dubai, Germany, Spain and Singapore, with local collaborators enabling culturally tailored execution
- Flexible infrastructure - registered office in Mumbai plus two rented godowns (Vasai/Virar, Maharashtra and Bengaluru, Karnataka) and temporary godowns rented at or near event locations

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geographic concentration of sales in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka (Internal Risk Factor 1) — These three states contributed Rs. 3,556.30 lakhs / 68.21% of domestic revenue for the period ended February 28, 2026 (FY25: 74.79%; FY24: 80.44%; FY23: 85.40%). Operations are susceptible to local and regional factors - economic and weather conditions, natural disasters, demographic changes - and to social, political or economic disruption, natural calamities, civil disruption, changes in state/local/central government policy or adverse competitive developments in those states. The Company states it has not experienced such an adverse impact as of the period ended February 28, 2026 or in the last three Fiscals, but gives no assurance for the future.
- Dependence on third-party outsourced subcontractors, with no executed registered formal arrangements (Internal Risk Factor 2) — Booth fabrication and related services are outsourced. The Company states it does not have any executed registered formal arrangements with such outsourced subcontractors governing matters such as specification of products, quality standards to be maintained, sales estimates and packaging of products. The risk factor text is truncated mid-sentence in the routed extract.
- Industry and market data is from a commissioned, paid-for report — All industry and market information in the Business and Risk Factors sections is derived from the Dun & Bradstreet Report, which was commissioned by and paid for by the Company for the purpose of the Offer - a stated conflict/reliance caveat.
- Operational performance indicators are unaudited and non-comparable — The DRHP states that various operational performance indicators may not be derived from the Restated Financial Statements, may not have been subjected to audit or review by the Statutory Auditor, and that their calculation method may vary from that used by other companies; investors are cautioned against undue reliance.
- Promoter concentration / low pre-Offer float — Promoters hold 1,06,75,996 Equity Shares constituting 94.55% of the pre-Offer issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share capital, and both Promoters are also selling shareholders in the Offer for Sale (up to 8,00,000 shares combined). Stated as fact in the Promoters and Objects sections; the DRHP text provided does not present this as a numbered risk factor.
